purpose: Rebuild the Windows Office, PDF, OCR and drawing payload with the recorded runtime versions.

artifacts.verification: Downloaded official archive and calculated SHA-256; installed runtime reports Python 3.11.9.

artifacts.license: Apache-2.0; bundled DLLs retain their respective licenses
artifacts.verification: SHA-256 calculated from the preserved downloaded installer; filename and upstream URL verified against the publisher page.
artifacts.notes: Extract the installer without installing it; retain its DLLs, doc directory and tessdata/configs/tsv. Add the two separately pinned language files below.

artifacts.verification: Publisher checksum matches the existing drawing builder pin and installed drawing manifest.

lockfiles.install: pip install -r requirements.lock in a dedicated venv, separate from the Office runtime

external_requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, PowerShell 7, Git, Rust MSVC toolchain and Visual Studio C++ Build Tools with a Windows SDK
Node.js 22 or newer compatible version with npm and a development Python 3.11 x64 with pip (the embeddable runtime does not provide pip)
A separately licensed local Microsoft Office installation exposing Word, Excel and PowerPoint COM APIs for native document workflows

Install model CLIs on each Runner computer, authenticate with that user account, then explicitly configure and validate its local execution resources. Never transfer account state, API keys, resource approvals or local Runner configuration.
limits: Version locks preserve selected dependency versions; Python wheel bytes are not hash-pinned in the existing requirements.lock files.
Upstream main URLs are accepted only when their bytes match the recorded SHA-256; a hash mismatch must stop the build.
This inventory preserves functionality prerequisites, not pre-existing accounts, personal documents, runtime databases or byte-identical Rust executable output.
